title: Android 低内存全景：RAM、ZRAM、kswapd、PSI 与 LMKD
key_conclusions: Android low-memory analysis connects app bucket growth to process PSS/RSS, system available memory, reclaim, ZRAM, PSI stalls, and LMKD decisions.
Java Heap, Native Heap, Graphics, dma-buf, and shared mappings can all become system pressure even when only one bucket looks suspicious locally.
LMKD analysis requires kill reason, adj, RSS/PSS, and pressure context, not only the victim process name.
Optimization must lower system pressure, reclaim/swap/stall evidence, or kill risk, not just one app heap number.
shallow_points: The article does not include real meminfo, vmstat, PSI, zram, procrank, or lmkd logs from a device.
It does not validate metric names and lmkd log formats across Android versions and vendor ROMs.
It does not include a Perfetto trace showing kswapd, direct reclaim, PSI, and app workload alignment.
It does not quantify thresholds for low-memory decisions on different RAM classes.
discovered_connections: Day 47's process bucket boundaries become the input side of system-wide memory pressure.
Day 46's Graphics/dma-buf boundary is necessary because shared buffers can pressure the system even when Java Heap is stable.
Day 49 should deepen page reclaim with file pages, anon pages, LRU, and MGLRU.
Day 54 and Day 57 should reuse the PSI and LMKD evidence chain.
The low-end memory special track begins here with a system-wide evidence model.
